question: If $A x^3+B x y=4$ (A and B are arbitrary constants) is the general solution of the differential equation $F(x) \;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}+G(x) \;\frac{d y}{d x}-2 y=0$ , then $F(1)+G(1)=$ [AP EAPCET 27 May 2025 S1]

solution: Solution: Solve the implicit general solution for $y$ . Assuming $B\ne 0$ , from $A x^3+Bxy=4$ we get $y=\frac{4-Ax^3}{Bx}=\frac{4}{B}\frac{1}{x}-\frac{A}{B}x^2.$ Set $c_1=\frac{4}{B}$ and $c_2=-\frac{A}{B}$ , so the general solution is $y=\frac{c_1}{x}+c_2x^2.$ Differentiate twice: $y'=-\frac{c_1}{x^2}+2c_2x,\qquad y''=\frac{2c_1}{x^3}+2c_2.$ Substitute these into $F(x)y''+G(x)y'-2y=0$ : $F(x)\left(\frac{2c_1}{x^3}+2c_2\right)+G(x)\left(-\frac{c_1}{x^2}+2c_2x\right)-2\left(\frac{c_1}{x}+c_2x^2\right)=0.$ Since $c_1$ and $c_2$ are arbitrary, their coefficients must separately vanish. For $c_1$ : $\frac{2F(x)}{x^3}-\frac{G(x)}{x^2}-\frac{2}{x}=0.$ Multiplying by $x^3$ gives $2F(x)-xG(x)-2x^2=0.$ For $c_2$ : $2F(x)+2xG(x)-2x^2=0,$ or $F(x)+xG(x)-x^2=0.$ Adding the two simplified equations gives $3F(x)-3x^2=0$ , so $F(x)=x^2$ . Then $F(x)+xG(x)-x^2=0$ gives $xG(x)=0$ , so $G(x)=0$ . Therefore $F(1)+G(1)=1^2+0=1.$ Thus the correct option is option A. © examsnet.com

question: What is the major product Y in the following reaction sequence? [AP EAPCET 27 May 2025 S1]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: The starting compound is benzamide, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}$ . Treatment with $\mathrm{C_6H_5SO_2Cl}$ in pyridine at $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$ dehydrates the primary amide to give benzonitrile, so $X = \mathrm{C_6H_5CN}$ . Acidic hydrolysis with $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ converts the nitrile into benzoic acid, $\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH}$ . Electrophilic bromination with $\mathrm{Br_2/FeBr_3}$ then occurs on the aromatic ring. The $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group is a meta-directing deactivator, so bromine enters the meta position. Therefore, the major product $Y$ is $3$ -bromobenzoic acid (meta-bromobenzoic acid). © examsnet.com
